Real registered installations route the latest committed group extension to both live push generations; a third non-FCM installation independently reads the same authorized activity cursor. The actual persisted group first mutation resolves to its parent boundary in the current play. An opponent action followed by the original actor starts a distinct group.

Injected SQL failure on game_outbox after hint creation rolls back gameplay mutation/group/final result/hints. A new ServiceRuntime executes the already-admitted original exactly once after restart, retaining one group activity and push intent; original retry still returns the same final result.

Existing affected server tests pass account/session registration, password-reset cleanup, invitation atomicity, HTTP authentication, retention/reset paging, push quiet/max10/retry/TTL and invalid-token fallback assertions. These were executed because GameService/ActivityService/ActivityHttp inputs changed, not claimed as new native/provider coverage.

Production ActivityWindowStore policy tests execute persisted pending first/due times and cursor, restart, duplicate push-fetch overlap without quiet-window reset, exact 2-second quiet and 10-second maximum boundaries, post-alert silent extension, next-group alert under the same per-game key, invitation independence, independent installation policies, foreground suppression versus background, summary-reset suppression, denied controls and stale-binding/storage-failure fences.

The same ActivityRefresh driver called by ActivityWorker executes real ActivityApi registration/page codecs against an owned Ktor HTTP mock and rejects an account change after fetch before local apply. Normal WorkManager wiring persists windows with the cursor and schedules a network-required deadline refresh; host tests do not execute Android scheduling.

Normal LobbyController asynchronous routing consumes the exact captured ActivityRoute, authorized group/play/parent boundary or invitation attempt; current-head replacement of an invitation downgrades to explicit current fallback. Deleted/unavailable results return to current Games. Route parsing retains kind/identity/account/binding rather than only game ID. The existing normal route/lifecycle supplies ActivityDisplay; no notification submits a board/invitation request or read receipt.

One combined affected pass: 13 server, 18 Android host and 1 protocol tests, zero failures/errors, plus normal non-FCM APK and all affected instrumentation Kotlin compilation. Instrumentation was authored/compiled only; no devices were used. Exact nine-suite JUnit bytes are retained. No clean/full-suite or repeated green broad check was run.
